notes:
Background: Nightingale is a London-headquartered legal-tech company building an internal enterprise search + contract analytics product for UK/EU law firms and in-house legal teams. Priority is strict UK/EU data residency and low query latency for lawyers (interactive search experience).

Timeline / recent activity:
- 2024-08-21: Intro call (Ava) — high level needs, sample corpus size ~120M documents (contracts, precedents, memos). Interested in RAG + reranking flow.
- 2024-09-03: Technical deep-dive with Marcus (SE) and infra team — discussed ingest pipeline, S3 connectors, and existing Pinecone POC.
- 2024-09-25: Sent sample dataset s3://nightingale-sample (anonymized). SE ran baseline embed + ANN probe.
- 2024-10-12: Fireflies call (ff_20241012_8234) — security checklist and residency questions. Customer: "If data leaves UK jurisdiction we can't proceed."
- 2024-11-05: Demo (hosted) showing candidate recall + rerank chain. Logged hosted API p95 latencies ~180ms for 3-stage pipeline (embed->ANN->rerank), cost estimate ~€0.007/query for current config.
- 2024-11-28: Onsite meeting w/ legal ops — discussed procurement timeline and commercial terms.

Technical requirements / success criteria (customer stated):
- Indexing scale: target initial index ~120M doc units (after shingling ~450M vectors). Need guidance on sharding & storage.
- Query latency: interactive goal p95 <= 150ms for default searches in UK region, failover p95 <= 250ms from EU region.
- Reranking: affordable hybrid rerank (top-50 candidates reranked) with end-to-end latency <= 200ms.
- Cost target: target cost per query <= €0.004-€0.006 at production scale (must account for embedding + ANN + rerank).
- Model preferences: prefer open models or customer-approved foundation models; support for quantized serving and smaller rerank models is attractive.
- Routing/failover: multi-region active-passive with sticky routing to UK for residency; automatic failover to eu-west with audit trail and documented data flow.
- Compliance: SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS integration, SOC2/ISO preference; formal Data Processing Addendum required.

POC plan discussed (next steps we own):
- P0: Confirm NW peering windows and estimate time-to-provision for a private (VPC) deployment in eu-west-2 (London).
- P1: Run indexing benchmark (sample 10M vectors) on Dedicated GPU pool — measure batch index throughput, storage footprint, and shard counts.
- P2: Run end-to-end query benchmark: measure embed latency, ANN recall, top-50 rerank latency (target <=200ms). Provide detailed token-level cost breakdown.
- P3: Provide a failover demo (eu-west -> eu-west-1) with logs and routing policy example.

Open questions / blockers (customer):
- "Can we guarantee that embeddings and reranks for UK-resident data never traverse non-UK endpoints?" — need documented network/data flow and PSO signoff.
- Dedicated pricing cadence: they want a 3-year reserved pricing option vs. pay-as-you-go.
- KMS/HSM specifics for UKKeyVault — customer will provide compliance checklist.

Notes from SE benchmark (Marcus):
- Baseline hosted embed (open-quant) gave 25ms median embed in eu-west-2; rerank model (distil-rank) median 60ms on a single A10-backed pod. ANN recall acceptable at 50NN.
- Suggested configuration: shard count 48 for 450M vectors, use on-disk quantization + memory caching for hot shards.

Attachments / references: pricing deck + security scope in drive links above. Jira tickets created for peering and benching: RINF-3421 (peering), RINF-3478 (benching).

Sales notes (short):
- Champion: CTO (Marta O.) — cares about residency and procurement.
- Economic sensitivity: high — likely to push for multi-year commit if price per query meets target.
- Next call: 2024-12-05 to confirm peering window and POC schedule.
